To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a hierarchical triple star with the following parameters: the primary and secondary stars have masses of 0.24+/-0.01 and 0.20+/-0.02Mcircle-dot and radii of 0.22+/-0.03 and 0.22-0.03Rcircle-dot, respectively.

the eclipsing binary in the hierarchical triple KOI 928 has an orbital period of 4.98829 days and that the total mass of this binary system is 0.424± 0.017Mcircledot, which is consistent with the masses of other low-mass eclipsing binaries in the Kepler field.

we have identified a new type of hierarchical triple star system where a low mass binary orbits a more mass third star, and that the eclipse timing variations provide information about the dynamics and the masses of the stars in the system. © 2014.

the hierarchical triple KOI 928 is composed of a 0.424Mcircle-dot binary in an 8.5 day orbit about a 1.3Msun tertiary star.
this is the first hierarchical triple star eclipsing binary system discovered by the NASA Kepler mission.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the eclipse timing variations seen due to the orbital motion of the binary about its tertiary provide the first opportunity to determine the mass and orbit of the eclipsing binary in a hierarchical triple star.
we have determined the masses and radii of two stars and the orbital parameters for a hierarchical triple star.
the eclipse timing variations of KOI 928 are consistent with the binary orbit being circular, with a mass of 0.423Mcircle-dot, and with a period of 4.98829 days.

eclipse timing variations can be used to determine the total mass of a binary and the mass function for a hierarchical triple system.
